Le potlatch.origine: Northwest Coast of North America (Kwakiutl, Haida)
Le potlatch.savoir: Among these peoples, rank is established not by accumulating but by giving, sometimes by publicly destroying more goods than one's rivals. Prestige goes to the most generous, not the richest.

La kula.savoir: Shell necklaces and armbands, with no practical use or market value, circulate from island to island over thousands of kilometers. They are never kept: to own them is to pass them on, forming lifelong alliances along the way.
La kula.lecon: You don't own a bond. You keep it in circulation.

Le hau.savoir: The Maori say that a gifted thing contains the hau, the spiritual power of the giver, which always seeks to return to its origin. It is this breath, attached to the object, that obliges the receiver to give back.
Le hau.lecon: What you are given keeps a part of the one who gave it.

Le moka.origine: Melpa, highlands of Papua New Guinea
Le moka.savoir: There, importance is gained not by what you own but by what you distribute. Giving more than can be returned puts the other in debt, and makes you a big man.
Le moka.lecon: Prestige is measured by what you have given, never by what you keep.

Le dāna.savoir: The selfless ritual gift, with no expectation of return, is held to elevate the giver. Giving purifies and frees: it is as much a spiritual act as a social one.
Le dāna.lecon: Giving without expecting is not impoverishing yourself: it is rising.

La Morgengabe.savoir: The morning gift was handed to the bride the day after the wedding, before witnesses. Its value far exceeded what custom required: the bond was sealed by excess, not by fair exchange.
La Morgengabe.lecon: A bond is sealed by what you give beyond what you owe.

Le nexum et le wadium.savoir: Long before our contracts, a handed-over object was enough to bind two people lastingly. The pledge was not a material guarantee: it carried a part of the one who pledged it. Our contracts descend, quite literally, from a gesture of giving.
Le nexum et le wadium.lecon: Our contracts are old gifts that have forgotten where they came from.

La xenia.savoir: Sacred Greek hospitality, placed under the protection of Zeus, required welcoming the stranger, feeding and protecting them before even asking their name. The bond of hospitality passed to descendants and committed families across generations.
La xenia.lecon: Welcoming the unknown was not a virtue: it was a sacred duty.

L'ubuntu.savoir: Ubuntu translates roughly as “I am because we are.” A person does not exist first alone, then in relation: they become themselves through their bonds with others.
L'ubuntu.lecon: I am fully myself only through others.

La dette.origine: David Graeber, Debt: The First 5,000 Years (2011)
La dette.savoir: Graeber shows that debt precedes money and barter, and that it is first a moral relationship between people before it is an amount. Reducing a debt to a figure to be repaid is already forgetting the bond it sealed.
La dette.lecon: Before it is a sum, a debt is a bond between two people.

Les communs.origine: Elinor Ostrom, Nobel Prize in Economics 2009
Les communs.savoir: It was believed that a shared resource was doomed to be plundered by everyone. Ostrom proved the opposite in real settings: communities govern their common goods lastingly, with neither market nor state, provided they give themselves rules of their own.
Les communs.lecon: Sharing doesn't lead to ruin. Badly governed sharing does.

L'encastrement.savoir: For almost all of history, the economy was embedded in society: a means serving bonds. The modern rupture is the moment when the market detaches itself and demands that society enter its order, rather than the reverse.
L'encastrement.lecon: The economy used to serve the bond. One day, it wanted the opposite.

Les trois formes d'échange.savoir: Polanyi distinguishes three ways humans have made things circulate: reciprocity (mutual giving), redistribution (through a center that gives back) and market exchange. The market is only one of the three. It simply ended up believing it was the only one.
Les trois formes d'échange.lecon: The market is only one of three ways to make things circulate. It is not the nature of things.

Le savoir commun.savoir: It isn't enough for everyone to know. Everyone must know that the others know, and know it in a cascade. It is this shared knowledge, not information alone, that makes a group able to act together.
Le savoir commun.lecon: A group acts not when everyone knows, but when everyone knows that the others know.

Communiquer n'est pas transmettre.nom: To communicate is not to transmit
Communiquer n'est pas transmettre.savoir: To communicate is to carry information through space, fast and wide. To transmit is to make something last through time, across people and generations. Most tools get a message across; few make a bond last.
Communiquer n'est pas transmettre.lecon: Getting a message across is easy. Making a bond last is a craft.

Le médium est le message.savoir: The form of a channel matters more than what it carries: it shapes the scale and form of our bonds. A tool that counts what everyone gives produces calculation; a tool that makes it visible without quantifying it produces recognition. Same content, two worlds.
Le médium est le message.lecon: The medium doesn't carry the relationship. It shapes it.

La sociabilité numérique.savoir: Against the received idea of a web that isolates, Casilli shows that it produces a new kind of sociability, with its own rules. And he rereads it through Mauss: online too, we post, share and reply, in cycles of gift and counter-gift.
La sociabilité numérique.lecon: The web doesn't destroy the bond. It makes another one, governed by the gift.

Les régimes de visibilité.savoir: On a platform, who sees what, who is highlighted, what stays hidden, is never neutral: it is a design choice. Design decides the shape of possible relationships. Making visible is already arranging the bond.
Les régimes de visibilité.lecon: Deciding who sees what is already deciding which relationships are possible.

La liminalité.origine: Arnold van Gennep and Victor Turner
La liminalité.savoir: Every rite of passage includes an in-between, the liminal phase, where you are no longer what you were and not yet what you will become. Turner sees it as the very place of transformation, and the birth of an intense bond among those who go through it together: communitas.
La liminalité.lecon: The threshold isn't something you cross to get somewhere else. It's where everything transforms.

L'expérience mémorable.origine: Pine and Gilmore, The Experience Economy (1999)
L'expérience mémorable.savoir: What we remember about a service is not its function, it's the moment it made us live. Value lies not in what is delivered, but in the experience that remains.
L'expérience mémorable.lecon: We forget what we were given. We remember what we lived.

La société de la fatigue.savoir: By turning everything into performance and activity, our age has erased contemplation, and exhausts itself. Han reminds us that stopping to look is not the opposite of acting: it is the condition of an action that makes sense.
La société de la fatigue.lecon: Contemplating is not doing nothing. It's what keeps action from being mere agitation.

Le care.savoir: Care, attention to others and to what makes them vulnerable, is neither a private nor a secondary matter: it is what holds every society together. We don't see it precisely because it works.
Le care.lecon: What takes care is invisible while it works, and vital when it's missing.

La confiance comme réducteur de complexi.nom: Trust as a reducer of complexity
La confiance comme réducteur de complexi.savoir: The world is too complex for us to verify everything. Trust is what lets us act despite uncertainty: a bet on the other that makes the future workable. Without it, nothing would circulate, because everything would have to be guaranteed in advance.
La confiance comme réducteur de complexi.lecon: Trust is what lets us act without verifying everything.

Le capital social.savoir: The wealth of a person or a group doesn't depend only on money or knowledge: it also depends on the network of relationships they can mobilize. The bond is a resource, and it is cultivated or squandered like any other.
Le capital social.lecon: Your relationships are capital. Invisible, but very real.

La reliance.savoir: To think is not only to distinguish and separate, it is to connect. Morin calls reliance the act of restoring the links that modern thought, by cutting everything into specialties, has severed. Understanding a complex world means connecting it, not fragmenting it.
La reliance.lecon: Modern thought excels at separating. It lacks the art of connecting.

Le passager clandestin.origine: Mancur Olson, The Logic of Collective Action (1965)
Le passager clandestin.savoir: In a group, everyone has an interest in benefiting from the common good without contributing, hoping that others will. If everyone reasons this way, nothing is produced. This is the problem every cooperation must solve in order to exist.
Le passager clandestin.lecon: The greatest danger to a common good is the one who benefits without contributing.

Le dilemme du prisonnier.savoir: Two people would gain by trusting each other, but each, afraid of being betrayed, chooses to betray: both end up losing, when cooperating would have served them. It is the very model of what blocks cooperation, for lack of trust and communication.
Le dilemme du prisonnier.lecon: Everyone tried to outsmart the other. Everyone lost. That's what happens without trust.

Les points de levier.savoir: In any system, there are places where a small action produces a big effect, and others where you can push hard and change nothing. The hardest part isn't acting: it's finding where.
Les points de levier.lecon: In a system, a light pressure in the right place changes everything.

Le lien avant le bien.savoir: In giving, what matters is never the object handed over, it's the relationship it opens, maintains or repairs. We think we exchange things; we exchange bonds.
Le lien avant le bien.lecon: It's never the good that matters. It's the bond it ties.

Qui, chez vous, donne quelque chose que.nom: Who, around you, gives something that nobody counts?
Qui, chez vous, donne quelque chose que.savoir: Welcoming a newcomer, defusing a tension, keeping the memory of a decision: this work appears on no dashboard. You only discover it the day it stops.
Qui, chez vous, donne quelque chose que.lecon: What isn't counted is often what holds everything together.

À qui devez-vous quelque chose que vous.nom: Whom do you owe something you will never quite repay?
À qui devez-vous quelque chose que vous.savoir: Advice, a door opened at the right moment: these debts can't be repaid, they are passed on elsewhere, to others. That's how a bond ends up holding a whole community together.
À qui devez-vous quelque chose que vous.lecon: The most beautiful bonds are the ones we never settle.

Qu'est-ce qui tiendrait encore, chez vou.nom: What would still hold, around you, if you left tomorrow?
Qu'est-ce qui tiendrait encore, chez vou.savoir: What rests on you alone is a dependency, not a system. What continues without you is what you have really passed on.
Qu'est-ce qui tiendrait encore, chez vou.lecon: A successful system is one that no longer needs you.

Quelle information ne remonte jamais, et.nom: What information never travels upward, and where is the missing ear?
Quelle information ne remonte jamais, et.savoir: When a problem never reaches the top, we blame those who stay silent. More often, there is simply no place to say it without risk.
Quelle information ne remonte jamais, et.lecon: Silence is rarely a flaw in people. It's a flaw in the channel.

Quel désaccord n'avez-vous jamais réussi.nom: What disagreement have you never managed to have?
Quel désaccord n'avez-vous jamais réussi.savoir: A subject we avoid doesn't disappear: it comes back in meetings that go in circles and decisions that don't stick. Being able to voice a disagreement is the sign of a solid relationship.
Quel désaccord n'avez-vous jamais réussi.lecon: A conflict we couldn't hold is a bond we couldn't repair.

Qu'est-ce qui circule chez vous sans que.nom: What circulates around you without anyone having decided it?
Qu'est-ce qui circule chez vous sans que.savoir: Mutual help between two departments, a channel where the real news travels: no org chart shows them. Yet that is often where the work really gets done.
Qu'est-ce qui circule chez vous sans que.lecon: What holds a collective together was almost never designed to.
